head: b23dc6d31942c9b748e997fbe3ee223b03d38f3d
classification_reasons: Spec tightness: tight - both of spec.md's flagged concerns (empty-input raises ValueError, parameter type is Collection[float]) are closed with a recorded decision (evidence/decisions-b.json items 1 and 2, item 2 explicitly marked overturned by the owner) and Acceptance is fully measurable (mean([1,2,3,4])==2.5, mean([5])==5.0, mean([]) raises ValueError, mean({1.0,2.0,3.0})==2.0, 9 passed, ruff clean, silent compileall).

Blast radius: small - the source diff touches exactly the files plan.md lists (sample_pkg/calc.py, sample_pkg/__init__.py, tests/test_calc.py) plus the change folder and status.yaml/plan.md bookkeeping; no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml), no sdlc.yaml risk_list item, no schema or config change; mean has no existing caller so add/divide/percent are unaffected.

Test coverage: mean is brand-new code with no pre-existing test covering it before this change - the build supplies its own four tests - so the third routine criterion (code the existing tests already cover) fails and the plan stays non-routine.
attempted: Intent: the diff adds mean(values) returning the arithmetic mean as a float, resolves the two open questions intent.md left (empty input -> ValueError, parameter type -> Collection[float]), exports it from __init__.py/__all__, and covers normal, single-element, empty and non-Sequence-Collection cases in tests/test_calc.py. This is exactly intent's Proposed outcome, nothing extra, nothing missing. The one intent item not in this diff - a proposed one-line CLAUDE.md Layout update - is explicitly scoped by intent/plan to the build PR description, not the repo, so its absence from the diff is expected, not a gap.

Spec and plan: verified calc.py's mean body (guard clause raising ValueError, then divide(sum(values), len(values)), collections.abc.Collection import) against plan.md step 1 verbatim, including the reconciled note that ruff's format-on-edit hook rewrote typing.Collection to collections.abc.Collection (plan.md was updated in this same phase-c diff to say so, so plan and diff agree at HEAD); __init__.py's import line and __all__ match step 2 exactly, alphabetically placed between divide and percent; the four tests in tests/test_calc.py match step 3's names and assertions exactly, including the set-based test pinning Collection[float]. No file changed outside plan.md's Files-that-change list.

Proof: compared verifier.md against the diff's four new tests. verifier.md names all four new tests individually (via 'pytest -k mean -v'), reports 9 passed consistent with the diff's added test count, and exercises exactly the behaviours spec.md/plan.md pin: empty raises ValueError (not ZeroDivisionError), a set (non-Sequence Collection) works, add/divide/percent are unaffected, and a generator is still rejected (via TypeError at len(), transparently noted as a detail the plan didn't spell out but not contradicted by it). A prior review of the previous HEAD (a94e11b) escalated because no test.log/build.log/lint.log were committed at phase c; I checked this independently against change 0001's own gate-c.json/gate-d.json (committed in this repo): gate (c) for 0001 recorded 'evidence present: verifier.md' as sufficient, and only gate (d) required 'evidence present: test.log, build.log, lint.log, verifier.md'. REVIEW.md's 'Do not report ... anything under changes/*/evidence/' also covers verifier.md's format directly. This independently confirms the panel's phase-c/phase-d scoping was correct, so I do not re-raise it.

Blast radius: mean is additive and uncalled elsewhere; divide is called, not modified; __all__ gains one name in the correct alphabetical slot. No guardrail file, no sdlc.yaml risk_list item (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config), no schema or config file appears in the diff. status.yaml's diff is only the phase/timestamp/panel_calls bump expected at this point in the workflow.

Policies: coding-standards' export-pattern and type-hint rules are met (Collection[float] hint, alphabetical import/__all__ placement matching add/divide/percent, no docstring inconsistency beyond the one plan.md itself flags and justifies); no new dependency, statistics.mean is not wrapped; security-baseline, ux-conventions and data-conventions are correctly inapplicable to a pure in-process arithmetic helper with no I/O, UI or stored data.

Tests: test_mean, test_mean_single_element, test_mean_empty and test_mean_accepts_non_sequence_collection each pin a distinct behaviour (correct averaging, single-element division, the explicit ValueError guard rather than a fallthrough ZeroDivisionError from divide, and the widened Collection[float]-not-Sequence contract via a set); manually traced each assertion against the guard-clause-plus-divide implementation and found no case where the bug (e.g. wrong exception type, Sequence-only implementation, off-by-one in the guard) would still pass. No pre-existing test (test_add, test_divide_by_zero_raises, test_percent, test_percent_zero_whole_raises, tests/test_flag.py) is touched or weakened by this feature-type change.
